answer: A bond-backed vouching web resists fake identities by making each new identity expensive: to join, an agent must lock a stake, and established agents who vouch for it share the risk — if the newcomer cheats, the vouchers lose their stake too. An attacker spinning up a spiral of sock puppets must fund every identity and every vouch, so the cost ripples outward with each fake, while honest agents keep the nectar of earned reputation and fees. One exposed fraud poisons the whole cluster, so scale stops paying.
